body_markdown:
## TL;DR


For a contact center already using CCaaS, when is native AI cheaper or easier than adding a voice AI layer, after counting provider costs, transfers, deployment, and verified resolutions? Compare both options against the same call mix and existing contract. Native AI may be the better choice if it uses capabilities you already pay for and avoids another telephony path; an add-on may be worth testing if it meets requirements the native option cannot. This is a cost and deployment worksheet, not another vendor ranking.


For a broad vendor shortlist, see the 11-provider[customer-service platform shortlist](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/best-ai-voice-customer-service-platforms) . For call-routing and use-case walkthroughs, see the[inbound automation workflow comparison](https://sigmamind.ai/blog/inbound-call-automation-comparison) . Here, the narrower question is whether your existing CCaaS platform’s native AI or a separate layer delivers the lower total cost for the same verified outcomes.


But here’s the problem most buyers discover too late: the price on the landing page is not the price on your invoice.


A per-minute platform fee is only one input. Ask each supplier which speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), language-model (LLM), carrier, transfer, and implementation charges are included in its quote. Include costs incurred on calls that transfer to a person or remain unresolved.


Use the same call mix, operating hours, transfer rules, resolution definition, and test period for both options. Compare incremental spend under your existing contract separately from total contracted spend, and verify the proposed call path before treating an integration as deployment-ready.


Request an itemized native-AI quote and an itemized add-on quote before committing budget. Test both on calls representative of your operation.


## Native AI vs. Add-On: Comparison Worksheet


Cost or deployment question CCaaS-native AI Add-on voice AI


Existing contract Record current licenses and committed spend; identify what is already paid for. Keep the CCaaS baseline visible; identify any contract or usage change caused by the add-on.


New AI charges Request AI add-on, usage, capacity, and support terms. Request platform, STT, TTS, LLM, carrier/SIP, and support terms.


Call path Verify routing, agent handoff, and available context in your deployment. Verify the first leg, transfer leg, context delivery, and who pays for each leg.


Launch and operation Price configuration, testing, QA, and ongoing changes. Price integration, testing, QA, and ongoing changes.


Outcome Divide comparable monthly cost by verified resolved calls. Use the same call mix and resolution rule.


## Criteria for an Existing CCaaS Deployment


First define the scope: which call intents, languages, hours, monthly volumes, and human-transfer conditions will both options handle? A cheaper quote is not comparable if it excludes difficult calls or shifts work to agents.


Apply these checks to both proposals:


**Conversation quality.** Test response time, interruptions, background noise, and recovery from misunderstood requests on representative calls. Ask for measurements from the proposed deployment path rather than relying on an unsourced universal latency threshold.


**Pricing clarity.** Separate published fees from variable usage charges and sales-quote items. Request the rate, billing unit, minimum, and payer for every layer; use the[voice AI cost-driver guide](https://www.sigmamind.ai/blog/no-visibility-into-cost-drivers-for-voice-ai-guide) to check the stack.


**Deployment path.** Ask for a diagram showing where the call enters, when AI takes control, how it returns to an agent, and what context reaches that agent. Confirm the exact path for your CCaaS tenant; a vendor integration label alone does not establish that your inbound first leg is supported.


**Handoff quality.** Test transfers in both proposals: confirm where the call lands, which identifiers or summaries reach the agent, whether the caller must repeat the request, and how both AI and human time are billed.


**Security and compliance.** Request current documentation and contract terms for your specific data and regulatory requirements. Do not assume a plan, integration, or workflow carries a particular certification.


**Operational effort.** Identify who builds and maintains each flow, who tests changes, and what implementation and QA work each option adds. Include those costs even when the software quote looks inexpensive.


## Where an Add-On Fits


### SigmaMind AI: Published Cost and Deployment Evidence


**Comparison role:** Quote SigmaMind AI as a possible add-on, then test its proposed call path against the CCaaS-native option. Do not assume that every CCaaS deployment or call direction has a documented integration.


**Published voice pricing:**[SigmaMind AI’s pricing page](https://www.sigmamind.ai/pricing) lists a **$0.04/min platform component** , plus STT, TTS, LLM, and telephony in its cost breakdown. Its $0.096/min pay-as-you-go voice headline is not a universal all-in rate for every configuration. Enterprise pricing requires a quote.


For this comparison, price the specific voice configuration and document how it connects to the existing phone system. A published platform component does not establish total call cost, and a demonstrated outbound transfer path does not establish an inbound first-leg deployment.


**Key features:**


- The[Five9 integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/five9-integration-guide.md) documents an **outbound** campaign transfer into SigmaMind AI, carrier-trunk or dedicated-PoP options, and handoff paths back to Five9 or into an inbound queue. Confirm configuration and context delivery for your deployment; it does not verify an inbound first leg.
- The[VICIdial integration guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) documents an **outbound** remote-agent SIP bridge and transfer architecture, not a general inbound CCaaS rollout.
- Published[Genesys](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/genesys.md) and[NICE](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/nice.md) pages are placeholders. Request direct verification of either proposed SigmaMind AI deployment before including it in a rollout plan.


**Proof to request:** Ask for results on calls matching your proposed use case, including transfer outcomes and independently checked resolutions. The published[refund-automation case study](https://www.sigmamind.ai/case-studies/ai-agent-handling-refunds-at-a-lower-cost) concerns a helpdesk/Shopify process, not verified voice customer-service calls.


**Honest tradeoffs:**


- Obtain the selected STT, TTS, LLM, and telephony rates alongside the $0.04/min platform component; identify any separate carrier or transfer charges.
- Confirm implementation, testing, QA, support, and contractual terms for the actual deployment.
- The pricing page says there is no separate concurrency fee. That is a billing term, not evidence of capacity at your required peak load.


Compare any add-on, including SigmaMind AI, only after mapping the proposed call and transfer legs. If the native AI already meets the same tested requirements at lower incremental cost or with less implementation work, keep the native option.

## Decision Matrix for Existing CCaaS Contracts


Start with the native AI available under your contract, then quote an add-on against the same scope. The rows below identify verification steps, not certified integration or price claims.


Existing platform Native AI first Add-on quote and test


Five9 Check contracted AI features, incremental fees, routing, and handoff. SigmaMind AI’s[guide](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/five9-integration-guide.md) documents an outbound transfer path. Verify the proposed direction, carrier legs, reclaim or queue handoff, and context; do not assume an inbound first leg.


Genesys Price available native AI against the existing contract and test agent handoff. Request an architecture and working test for any add-on. SigmaMind AI’s[Genesys page](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/genesys.md) does not document a deployment.


NICE CXone Price native AI and test routing and handoff within the contracted environment. Evaluate Cognigy separately and verify its proposed NICE integration. Require a working architecture for any other add-on; SigmaMind AI’s[NICE page](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/nice.md) is a placeholder.


Talkdesk Check native AI entitlements, usage, and the transfer path. Request a documented integration design and itemized quote for the chosen add-on; do not assume direct SigmaMind AI integration.


If an add-on is proposed for an outbound VICIdial operation, review SigmaMind AI’s documented[remote-agent SIP architecture](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) . Treat that outbound guide as evidence for the described path, not as proof of a general inbound integration.


Retell AI, Vapi, and Cognigy can also be quoted as add-on candidates where a proposed deployment is substantiated. Ask each for its complete cost stack, implementation owner, and a test of the exact transfer path; do not infer deployment fit from a vendor category.


A native option may win even when an add-on has an attractive platform rate: fewer new call legs, less integration work, or already-contracted capabilities can reduce incremental spend. Confirm those advantages in the quote and test rather than assuming either approach is cheaper.


An add-on may win if it resolves the same calls at lower comparable cost or supports a required path that native AI cannot. Count additional provider charges, transfers, integration work, and QA before reaching that conclusion.


Bring both quotes and the proposed call-path diagrams to procurement and operations review.[Talk to the SigmaMind team](https://www.sigmamind.ai/contact) if you want to scope an add-on test.


## What Voice AI Actually Costs in Production


Build two same-scope monthly scenarios: **A, use native AI within the existing CCaaS deployment; B, retain CCaaS and add a voice AI layer.** For each, itemize charges that change because of the project and show already-contracted spend separately. Request a sales quote wherever the rate is not published.


1. **Native scenario:** Record existing CCaaS licenses and committed spend separately; add incremental AI licenses, AI usage, carrier charges, transfers, implementation, QA, and human-agent time.
2. **Add-on scenario:** Keep the same CCaaS baseline; add the external platform, STT, TTS, LLM, carrier or SIP legs, transfers, implementation, QA, and human-agent time.
3. **Both scenarios:** Record minimums, support charges, taxes or other quoted charges where applicable, and who pays each provider. Match call mix, minutes, operating period, and resolution criteria.


For each scenario, calculate **monthly comparable cost = incremental AI and provider charges + incremental telephony and transfer charges + monthly allocated implementation and QA + human handling cost for transferred or unresolved calls** . Show existing contracted CCaaS spend alongside that figure; include it in both totals if the question is total contact-center spend rather than the incremental cost of this decision.


**Outcome measure: cost per verified resolved call**


**Cost per verified resolved call = monthly comparable cost ÷ calls verified as resolved under the same rule and observation period.** Count a call as resolved only after checking the agreed outcome in call records or the relevant system. Report transfers and unresolved calls separately: they still incur AI or telephony charges and may also incur human handling costs. Use actual invoices, provider rates, and sales quotes for the numerator, not an unsourced per-vendor estimate.


Compare the two results only after checking that both handled the same eligible calls. A lower cost per AI minute is not necessarily a lower cost per verified resolution if more callers transfer or need follow-up.


For the SigmaMind AI add-on scenario, use the published[$0.04/min platform component and pricing breakdown](https://www.sigmamind.ai/pricing) as a starting point, then price the selected STT, TTS, LLM, and telephony configuration. Confirm carrier and transfer legs in the proposed architecture. The $0.096/min pay-as-you-go headline is not a substitute for a configuration-specific total.


Do not use a market-average ROI as a substitute for your own pilot. Reconcile billed minutes and transfers with call records, verify resolved outcomes, and rerun the calculation using the call mix you expect to operate.


## Validate the Quote Before Deployment


**Confirm contract treatment.** Ask which native AI capabilities are already included, which require new licenses, and whether current minimum commitments offset usage. For an add-on, identify charges that continue under the CCaaS contract even when AI handles a call.


**Confirm billing units.** Establish whether each line is billed by minute, message, call, seat, transfer leg, or minimum commitment. A resolution-based performance measure does not mean the vendor invoices only for resolved calls.


**Test context at handoff.** Place calls that must transfer and check what the receiving agent actually sees. Include the transfer leg and subsequent agent work in cost, whether or not the AI produced a summary.


**Test exceptions.** Include callers who change intent, interrupt the agent, or request a person. Record whether each option reaches the right queue and preserves enough context for follow-up.


**Account for agent work.** Transfers, repeat contacts, and unresolved requests still consume human time. Ask operations to validate the handling time and follow-up work used in both cost scenarios.


Approve a rollout only after the proposed architecture, itemized quote, peak-load test, transfer test, and verified-resolution rule agree. If either option changes scope, rerun both scenarios on the revised scope.


## Make the Native-or-Add-On Decision


Choose the approach that meets your requirements with the lower comparable cost per verified resolved call and an acceptable deployment burden. Native CCaaS AI may win on already-contracted capabilities or a simpler call path; an add-on must justify its additional layers and transfer work with tested results.


If SigmaMind AI is on your add-on shortlist,[sign up to test it](https://dashboard.sigmamind.ai/p/signup) against your defined call mix and request a configuration-specific cost breakdown before rollout.


## FAQ


### What counts as a verified resolved call?


Define the intended outcome before the test, then check it in the call record or relevant business system. A call that ends without transfer is not automatically resolved. Apply the same rule and observation period to native AI and the add-on; report transferred and unresolved calls separately.


### Is the published per-minute price the total cost?


Not necessarily.[SigmaMind AI’s pricing page](https://www.sigmamind.ai/pricing) identifies a $0.04/min platform component and lists STT, TTS, LLM, and telephony as cost layers; its $0.096/min pay-as-you-go headline is not universal for every configuration. Request a scope-specific quote for other providers and include transfer and human costs when calculating cost per verified resolution.


### Do transferred calls count in the cost comparison?


Yes. Count AI usage and telephony up to transfer, any separately billed transfer leg, and the agent’s handling or follow-up work. Report the transfer rate alongside verified resolutions so a cheaper AI minute does not conceal more human work.


### How should I test conversation performance?


Use representative calls on the proposed telephony route, including interruptions, noisy audio, transfers, and expected peak load. Agree on measures with operations before testing and compare both options under the same conditions.


### How should I verify security and compliance?


Ask each vendor for current documentation, applicable plan terms, data-flow details, and any agreement your use case requires. Have security and legal teams review the proposed configuration before sensitive calls go live; do not infer compliance from a general product description.


### Is an advertised CCaaS integration enough to plan a rollout?


No. Ask for a diagram and test covering the first call leg, AI leg, agent transfer, context, and billing. SigmaMind AI documents[Five9 outbound handoff patterns](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/five9-integration-guide.md) and a[VICIdial outbound remote-agent architecture](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/vicidial-integration-guide.md) ; those guides do not verify every inbound path. Its[Genesys](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/genesys.md) and[NICE](https://docs.sigmamind.ai/nice.md) pages are placeholders, so verify either proposed deployment directly.


### What result should a pilot report?


Report eligible calls, billed AI minutes, verified resolutions, transfers, unresolved calls, subsequent human work, and total comparable cost for each option. Break results out by call type so a change in call mix does not masquerade as better performance.


### Should I choose native AI or an add-on?


Quote and test native AI first against your existing CCaaS contract. Test an add-on on the same calls when you need an alternative capability or cost structure. Choose only after comparing the verified call path, implementation effort, total monthly cost, and cost per verified resolved call; either option may win.
